title: The Essential tool for the trade
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：essential　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 essential 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the shopkeeper wrote of ① an essential tool for the trade in the account, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② more essential than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the shopkeeper, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the essential ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most essential tool for the trade anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the account for July 1970 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too essential to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the buyer who had come to help; the essential ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an essential point of the matter, and said that no buyer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as essential as the point of the matter they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was essential or not, and he said so.

By 1983 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the account. What the line asked for was ⑦ something essential, and nothing besides. The buyer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite essential; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the account kept the names of the essential ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1986, for the whole place, she wrote of another essential tool for the trade in the same account, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ more essential than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most essential point of the matter in the whole shop, she said in 1988, was the one she could never quite name; the essential ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 必不可少（前置定语 an essential tool for the trade：1976 年掌柜在账本里记下的那件必不可少的必备工具）
B. adj. 必不可少／本质（比较级 more essential than：文中两处，一处比这一行的必备工具，一处比预想）
C. adj. 必不可少／本质（最高级 the most essential：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 必不可少（表语 too essential to do：母亲觉得它太必不可少，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 本质（前置定语 an essential point of the matter：叔叔把整件事称作一桩本质的要害）
F. adj. 本质（同级比较 as essential as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩事情的要害相比）
G. adj. 本质（后置定语 something essential：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 本质（受程度副词修饰 quite essential：那位买主的评价）

items.q: an essential tool for the trade
the most essential tool for the trade anybody
an essential point of the matter
The most essential point of the matter in

answers.why: essential 意为“必不可少”，1976 年掌柜在账本里记下的是“一件必不可少的必备工具”，此处作前置定语 an essential tool for the trade。
essential 意为“必不可少”，此处用比较级 more essential than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
essential 意为“必不可少”，账本上 七月 那行字说它是铺子里最必不可少的一件，故用最高级 the most essential tool for the trade。
essential 意为“必不可少”，母亲认为这件东西“太必不可少了，谁也用不上”，too essential to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
essential 意为“本质”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩本质的要害”，此处作前置定语 an essential point of the matter。
essential 意为“本质”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩事情的要害一样本质”，同级比较用 as essential as。
essential 意为“本质”，账本上那半行字要的是“本质的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something essential。
essential 意为“本质”，邻铺子来的那位买主认为这套计划“相当本质”，quite 修饰原级 essential。
essential 意为“本质”，1986 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要本质”，故用比较级 more essential than。
essential 意为“本质”，母亲 1988 年说的是“整个铺子里最本质的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most essential point of the matter。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1976 年，掌柜在账本里记下了一件必不可少的必备工具。（an essential tool for the trade）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更必不可少。（more essential than …）
母亲觉得它太必不可少，谁也用不上。（too essential to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩本质的要害。（an essential point of the matter）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩事情的要害一样本质。（as essential as …）
到了 1983 年，账本上只剩半行字：要的是一件本质的东西。（something essential）
answers: In 1976 the shopkeeper wrote of an essential tool for the trade in the account.
Everybody said it was more essential than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too essential to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an essential point of the matter.
He said nobody would call it as essential as the point of the matter they had once had.
By 1983 the account asked for nothing but something essential.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 essential 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the shopkeeper wrote of an essential tool for the trade in the account, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most essential tool for the trade in the shop, or so the account says.
My mother thought it too essential to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an essential point of the matter, and nobody argued with him.
The buyer from the next shop called the plan quite essential, and everybody laughed.
The essential ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
